keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Northern March; its Kingdom of Germany shape draws the whole Elbe line as one). The page gives no extent and no area; the Altmark circle (Stendal, Salzwedel) and the Brandenburg circle (the Hevelli land conquered 928-29) are the researcher's reading. Overlaps the Billung March to the north (vassal tint in stem-duchy-of-saxony) and the Lutici to the east.

German expansion stalled until the Lutician alliance collapsed in the mid-11th century.

ledger.note: 965: Gero the Great dies and Otto divides his marches into five commands, one the Northern March. 'Dietrich of Haldensleben was margrave from 965 to 983'; infobox 'Northern March: 965-983'. The page names neither a border nor a capital.

region.text: the Brandenburg district on the Havel, the Hevelli land

ledger.note: 983: the Lutici-led rebellion destroys the march. The rebellion 'led to the factual disestablishment of the Northern March, though titular margraves were still appointed'; Lothair I (Walbeck) is margrave 983-1003. The Brandenburg lands are the ones taken; the Altmark is a reading.
1056: the Udonids take the march. Lothair Udo I of the House of Udonids, 1056-1057; Lothair Udo II 1057-1082; the Plötzkau margraves Helperich (1112-1114) and Conrad (1130-1133) follow.

1134: Albert the Bear is invested with the Northern March. His services 'were rewarded in 1134 by the investiture of the Northern March, which was again without a ruler'; he renounced Saxony in 1142 and took part in the Wendish Crusade of 1147.

region.text: the Brandenburg district on the Havel, the Hevelli land

ledger.note: 1150: Albert the Bear secures the Brandenburg district. 'Albert secured this district when the prince died in 1150', by an arrangement with Pribislav-Henry, the last Hevelli ruler (the page calls it an arrangement, not a will). ledger.note: 1157: the Northern March becomes the March of Brandenburg. Albert's expanded march, now including the Slavic lands around Brandenburg, 'became a hereditary possession and was called the March of Brandenburg'; Albert 'became the founder of the Margraviate of Brandenburg in 1157' and died on 18 November 1170.

notes: Two pages opened (budget 2-5). The Northern March page has no extent, area or capital; both circles are the researcher's. The page's infobox gives 965-983 as the march itself and treats 983-1157 as a titular and rump period; the dossier keeps the rump to 1157 so that Brandenburg's start is continuous. The 1157 Brandenburg period to 1259 (Cliopatria's Margraviate of Brandenburg begins 1260) has no dossier: eu-09's margraviate-of-brandenburg dossier should start from this one's end and cover Albert's expansion (Havelland, Teltow, Barnim, Uckermark: undated on the Albert page). Not settled: Altmark vs Brandenburg after 983; Hevelli (Pribislav-Henry) as a state; 1114-1130 margrave gap. Counterparts needing dossiers: March of Gero, Hevelli, margraviate-of-brandenburg (eu-09). Gazetteer lacks Stendal, Salzwedel and Brandenburg an der Havel (coordinates used).
